summary:
LUNA-AI, developed by TEMREN Space Team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, is an interactive decision-support platform designed to make lunar landing site selection safer, more efficient, and data-driven.
Focusing on the Mons Mouton region near the Moon’s South Pole, LUNA-AI combines an interactive 3D lunar model with detailed 2D terrain analysis. Users can select a landing date and time to evaluate potential landing sites based on critical parameters, including terrain slope, surface roughness, solar illumination, energy availability, Earth communication visibility, and environmental hazards.

By integrating NASA's LOLA elevation data, LROC imagery, and SPICE-based astronomical calculations, the system evaluates candidate locations and provides comparative safety and operational efficiency scores. Users can explore individual sites, examine detailed environmental conditions, and understand the factors influencing each recommendation.
Lunar landing site selection is challenging due to extreme lighting conditions, complex terrain, and communication limitations, particularly near the lunar poles. LUNA-AI addresses these challenges by transforming complex scientific data into accessible, actionable insights.
Our goal is to support informed landing site assessments and contribute to safer, more sustainable future lunar exploration.
details:
LUNA-AI — Detailed Project Description

LUNA-AI (Lunar Landing Site Navigation & Decision Support System) is an interactive, data-driven platform developed by TEMREN Space Team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project aims to simplify the complex process of evaluating potential lunar landing sites by combining scientific analysis, astronomical calculations, and intuitive visualization.

How Does LUNA-AI Work?

LUNA-AI focuses on the Mons Mouton region near the Moon's South Pole, an area of significant scientific interest due to its challenging terrain, unique illumination conditions, and potential access to valuable lunar resources.

The platform features an interactive 3D model of the Moon, allowing users to explore the lunar surface and locate Mons Mouton. Selecting the region opens a detailed 2D topographic map displaying candidate landing sites.

Users enter their preferred landing date and time, triggering an evaluation of each candidate location based on key environmental and operational parameters:

  • Terrain Safety: Surface slope, elevation variations, roughness, and potential geological hazards.
  • Solar Illumination: Sun position, illumination duration, and possible terrain-induced shadows.
  • Energy Availability: Estimated solar energy potential and periods of limited sunlight.
  • Earth Communication Visibility: Geometric line-of-sight between the landing site and Earth.
  • Operational Feasibility: Environmental constraints, accessibility, and potential mission risks.

The system combines these parameters to calculate comparative safety and operational efficiency scores. Candidate sites are ranked according to their suitability, while detailed information panels allow users to examine individual locations and understand the factors influencing their scores.

Technologies and Scientific Data

LUNA-AI integrates publicly available NASA scientific datasets with computational analysis and web-based visualization technologies.

The project's primary data sources and technologies include:

  • NASA LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter): Digital elevation models for terrain analysis and slope calculations.
  • LROC (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera): Lunar surface imagery supporting geographic interpretation and hazard assessment.
  • NASA/JPL SPICE: Astronomical geometry calculations for determining the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to lunar landing sites.
  • Python: Scientific calculations, data processing, environmental analysis, and landing-site evaluation.
  • NumPy and geospatial processing tools: Numerical analysis and processing of lunar elevation data.
  • Web-based 3D and 2D visualization technologies: Interactive lunar exploration, geographic visualization, and presentation of evaluation results.
  • GitHub: Source code management and collaboration throughout development.

The project is primarily software-based and does not require a physical lunar rover or specialized aerospace hardware for its current implementation.

Innovation and Creativity

LUNA-AI's main innovation is its integration of multiple scientific and operational factors into a single, accessible decision-support environment.

Instead of presenting static lunar maps or isolated datasets, the platform enables users to investigate how the suitability of a landing site changes with the selected date and time.

Its combination of global 3D exploration, regional 2D terrain visualization, dynamic environmental evaluation, comparative scoring, and explainable recommendations creates an interactive experience that connects scientific research with practical mission planning.

The project also draws lessons from previous lunar missions, including Intuitive Machines' Odysseus and Athena landers, to emphasize the importance of landing safety, terrain assessment, and environmental awareness.

Challenges and Factors Considered

The team considered several major challenges associated with lunar south polar exploration:

  1. Extreme lighting conditions: Low solar elevation angles and terrain shadows can significantly affect available energy.
  2. Complex topography: Slopes, craters, and irregular surfaces can introduce serious landing hazards.
  3. Communication limitations: Terrain obstruction and changing Earth visibility can restrict direct communication.
  4. Time-dependent conditions: A location suitable at one time may become less favorable during another operational period.
  5. Scientific data reliability: Dataset resolution, coordinate accuracy, and environmental uncertainty must be considered when interpreting results.

To address these challenges, LUNA-AI emphasizes transparent evaluation criteria, comparative analysis, and the use of established scientific data sources.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNA-AI is designed to make lunar landing site analysis more understandable and accessible to students, researchers, engineers, educators, and space enthusiasts.

By bringing together terrain information, illumination predictions, communication visibility, and operational constraints, the platform helps users identify potentially suitable landing locations and recognize the trade-offs involved in mission planning.

Our long-term vision is to develop LUNA-AI into a more comprehensive lunar mission planning and educational tool, supporting additional regions, mission configurations, and environmental parameters.

LUNA-AI represents our vision of transforming complex lunar science into understandable, interactive, and actionable information—contributing to more informed decisions and a safer, more sustainable future for lunar exploration.
